title: Akshay Kumar Is Making India's First Alien Thriller. The Creature Designer Built the Actual Xenomorph.
excerpt: Samuk brings Alec Gillis — the man behind Alien, Predator, and Prey — to Bollywood. Practical creatures, limited VFX, and a 2027 release that could reset what Indian genre cinema looks like.
body:
Somewhere in a production office in Mumbai, there is now a binder full of creature sketches that would make Ridley Scott do a double take. Akshay Kumar has signed on to star in Samuk, and if even half of what producer Vipul Amrutlal Shah is promising comes true, Indian cinema is about to have its Alien moment.

The film is being described as India's first full-scale alien action thriller — not a comedy with an alien subplot, not a VFX-heavy spectacle that looks like a video game cutscene, but a survival horror film built on the same principles that made Alien and Predator feel terrifyingly real. And the team behind it is not messing around.

The Hollywood Connection That Changes Everything

Alec Gillis — the creature FX designer who built the Xenomorph for Alien 3, designed the Predator for Prey (2022), and has spent four decades making monsters that haunt your sleep — is designing and building the creature for Samuk. Let that sink in. The man who literally constructed the most iconic movie monster in cinema history is now working on a Bollywood film.

This is not a consulting gig or a remote advisory role. Gillis will design, sculpt, and bring the alien creature to life using practical effects — the kind you can touch, the kind that bleeds on set, the kind that makes actors genuinely flinch during takes.

"We have opted for old-school filmmaking, which means we are going to shoot as much as possible practically and live on set. The use of VFX will be very limited. That is how you get it absolutely bang-on." — Vipul Amrutlal Shah

Director Kanishk Varma, who previously helmed Sanak and Glory, conceived the project from his obsession with elite security forces and sci-fi horror. "I wanted the creature to feel physically real on set," Varma said. "Old-school tactile horror is what made films like Alien timeless."

Why This Matters for the Diaspora

For NRI audiences who grew up watching Hollywood creature features and always wondered why Bollywood never attempted the genre seriously — this is the answer. Indian cinema has dipped its toes into sci-fi before (Koi... Mil Gaya, PK, Brahmastra), but always with a comedic or mythological wrapper. Samuk is promising something different: a genre film that plays by international horror rules, with a creature built to the same standard as anything in the Alien franchise.

This shift in genre could resonate deeply with the Indian diaspora, who often seek authentic and thrilling cinematic experiences that reflect global standards. The success of Samuk could pave the way for more serious genre films in India, potentially influencing remittance flows as NRIs may be more inclined to support films that reflect their tastes and expectations. Additionally, a successful release could strengthen cultural ties, as families abroad might connect over shared excitement for a film that breaks new ground in Indian cinema.

British stunt coordinator Luke Tumber, whose credits include Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning, Venom, and No Time to Die, is handling the action choreography. The international crew signals an ambition that goes beyond the domestic box office — this is a film designed to travel.

Shooting begins in August 2026, with a theatrical release planned for 2027.

Akshay's Genre Pivot

For Akshay Kumar, Samuk represents the most dramatic genre shift of a career that has already spanned comedy, patriotic drama, horror comedy (Bhool Bhulaiyaa), and action. After a rough stretch at the box office — where films like Bade Miyan Chote Miyan and Khel Khel Mein underperformed — the actor has been recalibrating.

His recent Bhooth Bangla, which just dropped on Netflix after a ₹264 crore theatrical run, proved he still has pull. But Samuk is a different beast entirely — literally. This is Akshay stepping into a space where there are no Bollywood benchmarks, no formula to fall back on.

"Alien thriller is a totally new genre for me and also for our films. I am very excited about it." — Akshay Kumar

Vipul Shah, who has worked with Akshay on Namastey London, Singh Is Kinng, and Holiday, revealed that the actor is deeply involved despite his packed schedule: "Despite being so busy, he's deeply involved. It's heartwarming."

The Real Question

Can an Indian film actually deliver creature horror at a Hollywood standard? Samuk's pedigree says yes — but the proof will be in the prosthetics. With Alec Gillis building the monster, Luke Tumber choreographing the chaos, and Kanishk Varma directing with a clear vision of practical-first filmmaking, this is the most internationally credentialed Indian genre film ever attempted.

If it works, it doesn't just give Akshay Kumar a comeback vehicle. It opens an entirely new lane for Indian cinema. And if the creature is half as terrifying as Gillis's previous work, you might want to skip the late-night solo viewing.
